values.formattedValue: How much can we afford to pay for a customer?
This sheet answers that question for every country we sell in, every morning.
Every order carries costs: the product, the shipping, the packaging, the payment fee, the returns. What's left is the most we can spend to win that order.
This sheet works out that figure for Nigeria, the UK, Canada and the US. It then compares it with what we actually paid in advertising for each order.

Paid less than we can afford? The country is making money. Scale it.
Paid more? Every order is losing money. Cut it.
1.   Enter your costs. Fill in the yellow cells on the Unit Economics tab. Update them when supplier or courier prices change.
2.   Choose a period. Last 30 days, last 90 days, year to date, or the last 12 months.
3.   Read the verdict. Scale, Hold or Cut, one for each country.
Allowable CAC   The most we can pay for an order and still break even.
Target CAC   The most we can pay and still hit our profit target.
Actual CAC   What we really paid. Ad spend in the country ÷ orders shipped there.
Profit per order after ads   What we keep. Green means profit. Red means we lose money on every order.
Ad spend from Meta. Orders and order values from Shopify. Both refresh every morning. Costs come from you.
Actual CAC counts every order shipped to a country, including repeat customers and orders that did not come from an ad. Each order is judged on its own, with no repeat purchase assumed.
What each order earns, what we can afford to pay Meta for it, and what we actually pay. Fill the yellow cells. The rest updates itself.
Target profit after ads (% of order)
SCALE  we pay less than target, spend more.     HOLD  profitable, below target.     CUT  every order loses money after ads.
